newsitem.title: UK: Copper seesaws around $2,100 in volatile LME trade.
newsitem.headline: Copper seesaws around $2,100 in volatile LME trade.

text.p: LME copper whipsawed on Tuesday after a more bullish than expected stocks report shook up the market as it approached the slow holiday period.
"That (stock data) caught the market by surprise. It showed the market was tighter than we thought," one senior floor trader said.
LME inventories increased by only 2,875 tonnes after some traders expected a rise of up to 12,000 tonnes.
Prices burst back above $2,100 resistance as traders rushed to cover shorts in the morning, hovered there in a narrow range in the afternoon, but slipped backed below $2,100 in late floor trading.
Three month copper finished the afternoon kerb at $2,095, up $14 and well above key $2,080 support.
It traded in a range of $2,077 to $2,118.

Many players had expected prices to drift to the $2,000 level or below in the traditionally slow period surrounding the western Christmas holidays after tight December dates had passed and the cash premium eased.
The cash/threes backwardation edged down $5 to $50.
"Now we could very well see prices hold above $2,000 and more tightness emerge in the New Year," another floor trader said, adding that some positions had been rolled over to February and March.
But traders were wary and broker Rudolf Wolff said in a commentary any confirmed breach of the $2,080 level would target $2,000 based on a head and shoulders pattern.
Any move above $2,100 would find resistance at $2,150.
Nickel consolidated after crumbling to fresh 26-month lows on Monday under the weight of speculative selling and weak fundamentals.
It ended at $6,575, up $65, but chartists said the damaged technical picture targeted falls to $6,400 in coming weeks.
Tin bounced from Monday's new 19-month lows, finishing the afternoon kerb at $5,830, up $145.
Analysts said the recovery from oversold levels may be temporary and if the market fails to build a base further weakness could take prices to $5,600 or $5,500.
Aluminium continued its independent path, gradually climbing higher amid the gyrations of the others.
Trade buying and forward orders in the physical market continue to buoy prices, analysts say.
Traders said a round of late short-covering on the kerb helped three month prices finish at $1,530, up $14.
Zinc ended up $10 at $1,055, a near-term resistance level, and lead finished the day firmer at $701 versus $689/90 on Monday.
Alloy was slightly stronger at $1,360/65 versus $1,357/60.
-- Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2936
